title: What Git Does Not Record: Provenance Legibility in Two AI-Assisted Research Repositories
abstract: arXiv:2610.28655v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Publishers and funders increasingly ask authors to disclose how AI tools contributed to a piece of research. In computational work the repository is where an author or an auditor would look for the answer, and we ask what it can actually supply. We audit two single-investigator repositories by the same author in the same field, each carrying a different class of agent residue: a prescriptive trace of standing rule files and a narrative trace of a running agent scratchpad, in repositories of 466 and 103 commits. The two are legible in opposite ways. 85.6% of the lines ever committed to the prescriptive trace are visible at the current revision, and a standing rule states a conclusion and discards the episode behind it; the narrative trace records episodes and shows 21.8%. translated_title: Git未记录的内容：两个AI辅助研究仓库中的溯源可读性
translated_abstract: 出版商和资助机构越来越多地要求作者披露AI工具在一项研究中发挥了何种作用。在计算类研究工作中，代码仓库正是作者或审计者寻求答案的地方，而本研究追问的是：仓库实际上能够提供什么。我们审计了同一作者在同一领域开展的两个单人研究仓库，每个仓库承载着不同类型的智能体残留痕迹：其一是常设规则文件构成的规范性痕迹，其二是持续运行的智能体草稿本构成的叙事性痕迹，两个仓库分别包含466次和103次提交。两者的可读性呈现相反的特征：规范性痕迹中曾经提交过的代码行有85.6%在当前修订版本中仍然可见，且常设规则只陈述结论而丢弃其背后的过程片段；叙事性痕迹记录了过程片段，但可见比例仅为21.8%。若按修订版本计数，差距则小得多：规范性痕迹的41个修订版本中有15个不留任何可见行，而叙事性痕迹的41个中有18个。
tldr: 本研究通过审计同一作者带有不同类型AI智能体残留痕迹的两个研究仓库，发现代码仓库在披露AI参与科研时的溯源可读性呈反向差异——规范性规则痕迹保留85.6%的结论性行但丢失过程片段，叙事性草稿痕迹记录过程片段却仅存21.8%——从而揭示了Git仓库无法完整回答“AI如何参与研究”这一溯源问题的根本局限。
en_tdlr: By auditing two AI-assisted research repositories carrying different classes of agent residue—prescriptive standing rule files versus a narrative agent scratchpad—this study reveals opposite patterns of provenance legibility (85.6% of prescriptive-trace lines persist at HEAD while only 21.8% of narrative-trace lines survive), demonstrating the fundamental limits of Git as a source for disclosing how AI tools contributed to research.
